cross_domain_analogy_scan.common_abstraction: A surrogate family can reproduce arbitrarily long finite prefixes of a target stream; a tail-stable functional transfers a sign violation to one surrogate.
disanalogies: quadratic-character global arithmetic is highly constrained; generic stream emulators do not encode class numbers or L-functions
cross_domain_analogy_scan.transferable_principle: Search for a prefix-complete good-surrogate subfamily, not necessarily universal goodness of all surrogates.
cross_domain_analogy_scan.validation_obligation: Prove the transfer with an explicit tail constant and source-family completeness; do not use analogy as theorem authority.

equivalent_representations: Conrey f(x)=sum_{n>=1} lambda(n) sin(2*pi*n*x)/n^2; f(x)>=0 on [0,1/4] implies RH.
For q≡3 mod 8 squarefree, f_q(x)=sum chi_q(n) sin(2*pi*n*x)/n^2.
Dirichlet class-number formula in Conrey's normalization: h(q)=S_q(q/2)=sqrt(q)/pi*L(1,chi_q).
For integer N, elementary Cesaro identity: S_q(N)=(1/N)*sum_{m=1}^{N-1} A_q(m), A_q(m)=sum_{n<=m} chi_q(n).

transfer_assumptions: Conrey Theorem 1 is accepted only at primary-source authority: f>=0 on [0,1/4] implies RH.
Prefix imitation is exact through N for the chosen q; no probabilistic approximation is substituted.
The f/f_q tail comparison uses only |lambda(n)|<=1 and |chi_q(n)|<=1, giving |f-f_q|<2/N once prefixes agree through N.
The character-side positivity premise is not inferred from numerics or from GRH for L(s,chi).
